title: Steam Pipes - Sizing
description: Calculate pressure drop and sizing for steam distribution pipes. Determines available pressure for distribution, major friction losses, minor losses in fittings, and equivalent pipe lengths.

components.content:
## Steam Pipe Sizing Calculator

The pressure available for distribution of steam is the pressure difference between the initial pressure at the boiler and the required final pressure at the steam consumer.

**Available Pressure Drop:** p = pj - pk

**Total Pressure Drop:** pt = pmajor + pminor

outputs.label: Pressure Drop per 100 ft
outputs.formula: 0.01306 * inputs.steam_flow_rate * inputs.steam_flow_rate * (1 + 3.6/inputs.pipe_inside_diameter) / (3600 * inputs.steam_density * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter)

outputs.label: Major Pressure Loss (Total Length)
outputs.formula: (0.01306 * inputs.steam_flow_rate * inputs.steam_flow_rate * (1 + 3.6/inputs.pipe_inside_diameter) / (3600 * inputs.steam_density * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter * inputs.pipe_inside_diameter)) * inputs.pipe_length / 100

components.content:
## Typical Steam Velocities

- **Exhaust steam:** 20 to 30 m/s (70 - 100 ft/s)
- **Saturated steam:** 30 to 40 m/s (100 - 130 ft/s)
- **Superheated steam:** 40 to 60 m/s (130 - 200 ft/s)

## Rule of Thumb

Total pressure drop is approximately 5-10% of initial pressure per 100 m of pipe.
